verses.1: A Psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son. LORD, how are they multiplied that trouble me? many are they that rise up against me.
verses.2: Many there are who say of my soul, There is no help for him in God. Selah.
verses.3: But thou, O LORD, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of my head.
verses.4: I cried to the LORD with my voice, and he heard me from his holy hill. Selah.
verses.5: I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me.
verses.6: I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set themselves against me on all sides.
verses.7: Arise, O LORD; save me, O my God: for thou hast smitten all my enemies upon the cheek bone; thou hast broken the teeth of the ungodly.
verses.8: Salvation belongeth to the LORD: thy blessing is upon thy people. Selah.

metadata.source: Derived from Webster's Bible (1833), revised as a poetic KJV-tradition translation filtered through the theology of abiding in Christ.
